extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for The BMJ (clinicians, researchers, healthcare professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for conducting peer review of manuscripts submitted to The BMJ, including general principles, open peer review policy, conflicts of interest, and detailed criteria for appraising research and other article types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The BMJ has fully open peer review for all articles which means the names of reviewers are disclosed to the author of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are asked to sign their reports and declare any competing interests. Accepted research and analysis papers will usually have their prepublication history posted alongside them, comprising prior manuscript versions, study protocol (mandatory for clinical trials), manuscript committee meeting reports, reviewers' comments, and authors' responses; this is posted at publication under the 'peer review' tab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer role and editorial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers advise editors, who make the final decision (aided by an editorial committee for research and most analysis articles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will be informed of decisions by email; if an article is not accepted, reviewer comments will still be passed on to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and licensing of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: You will remain the owner of the review you submit to us, but by submitting you agree to license your work to The BMJ for the purposes outlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If published, your review will be published under the same license as the article. It is your responsibility to obtain consent of any co-reviewer or other third party who contributed to your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: An author’s manuscript must remain confidential until it is published, and you must not disclose any information about an unpublished manuscript, including your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may state that you reviewed for the journal but must not post details of the article or any part of the review that would breach confidentiality. Do not contact authors directly; queries should go through the editorial office. If you discuss the manuscript with a colleague, ensure they understand confidentiality and do not disclose information until publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and acceptance of invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree to review only if you are able to return a review within the proposed or mutually agreed time-frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot review, suggest alternative reviewers based on expertise and without personal considerations or intention of a particular outcome. If you accept, meet deadlines or communicate inability promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: During the review process reviewers must declare any potentially conflicting or competing interests (personal, financial, intellectual, professional, political or religious).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer major concerns to the editorial office before beginning the review. The BMJ focuses its request on financial interests and asks specific questions before submitting reviews, including: reimbursement for attending a symposium; fees for speaking; fees for organising education; funds for research; funds for a member of staff; consulting fees; employment by organisations that may gain/lose financially in past five years; holdings of stocks/shares. If you have any competing interests please declare them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a fair, honest, and unbiased assessment of strengths and weaknesses; be professional and refrain from hostile, inflammatory, libelous, or derogatory personal comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific in critique and provide supporting evidence with appropriate references to substantiate general statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity and evidence in critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific in your critique and provide supporting evidence and appropriate references to substantiate general statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the work is unclear because of missing analyses, comment and explain what additional analyses would clarify the work. Cite relevant references when commenting on originality or gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not extend work beyond its scope
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not the job of the reviewer to extend the work beyond its current scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest reasonable additional analyses or clarifications but avoid demanding that reviewers perform or impose major new studies that change the paper's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-reviewer and third-party contributor consent and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain the consent of any co-reviewer or third party who contributed to your review and disclose their identity and any potential competing interests when submitting the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review owner must ensure co-reviewers are aware of confidentiality and disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript handling and destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not retain the manuscript for personal use and should destroy copies after submitting their review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all copies (digital and printed) are deleted/destroyed to maintain confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting suspected misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have concerns that misconduct occurred during research, writing, or submission, or you notice substantial similarity with another submission or published article, inform the journal editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report suspected fraud, plagiarism, or duplicate submission promptly to editors for investigation rather than addressing authors directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reporting checklists and protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Check documents in supplemental files (eg. reporting checklists such as CONSORT, PRISMA, STROBE) and the protocol for an RCT to ensure they match the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EQUATOR Network for reporting statements and extensions; verify that supplemental documents do not contain information that should be reported in the manuscript or that raise concerns about the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess overall importance
rubrics_metrics.description: For all articles, consider: Is the article important? Will it help readers make better decisions and, if so, how?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the practical impact on readers (clinicians, policymakers, educators, patients) and how the article would change decisions or practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess contribution to existing knowledge (originality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the work add enough to what is already in the published literature? If so, what does it add?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant references to support comments on originality and identify whether there are obvious prior publications the authors should have considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether a general medical journal is the right place for the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the importance of the work to The BMJ's general readership and whether specialist journals might be more appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research question clarity and appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the research question clearly defined and appropriately answered?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a clearly stated objective and assess whether the study design and analyses address that objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall study design adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the overall design of the study appropriate and adequate to answer the research question?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether methods, sampling, controls, and analysis plan are suitable to address bias and confounding and to support the conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants and representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are participants adequately described, their conditions defined, and inclusion and exclusion criteria given? How representative are the participants of the population affected by the evidence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider recruitment methods, baseline characteristics, and generalisability to clinical populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and outcomes reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Are methods adequately described? Is the main outcome measure clear? Is the study fully reported in line with the appropriate reporting statement or checklist?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check detailed methods for reproducibility, appropriateness of outcome measures, statistical analyses, and adherence to reporting guidelines (EQUATOR). Consider ethical conduct beyond mere IRB approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results credibility and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the results answer the research question? Are they credible and well presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity of tables/figures, whether analyses match methods, handling of missing data, and robustness/sensitivity analyses where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the interpretation and conclusions warranted by and sufficiently derived from/focused on the data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether authors discuss findings in light of previous evidence, avoid overstating implications, and present a clear message tied to the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: References completeness and currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Are references up to date and relevant? Are there any glaring omissions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out missing pivotal studies or inappropriate citations; recommend inclusion of key literature where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and key messages accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the abstract/summary/key messages/what this paper adds reflect accurately what the paper says?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency between abstract and main text and that key messages are supported by the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient and public reviewer perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Patients are asked to review articles from the patient perspective, focusing on importance and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patient reviewers should assess clarity, relevance to patients, and whether the paper addresses patient concerns; patient reviewer training materials are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting alternative reviewers ethically
rubrics_metrics.description: If you cannot review, it is helpful to suggest alternative reviewers based on their expertise without personal considerations or intention of a specific outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid suggesting reviewers with conflicts of interest or who might bias the process; suggest individuals qualified to provide objective appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback to the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: The BMJ welcomes feedback from reviewers about manuscripts reviewed and the review process in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have comments on a manuscript or the decision, contact papersadmin@bmj.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests policy focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The BMJ has chosen to restrict its request about competing interests to financial interests to improve disclosure rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the editorial 'Beyond conflict of interest' and the competing interests guidance for authors to understand the thinking behind the policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives for high-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: For the best reviews The BMJ offers up to 3 AMA PRA Category 1 CME points (in partnership with Cleveland Clinic Foundation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an incentive; reviewers should still follow the standards and criteria outlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial transparency and provenance statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The BMJ will add a statement of provenance to accepted articles indicating whether they were commissioned and whether they were externally peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include 'Not commissioned; externally peer reviewed', 'Commissioned; not externally peer reviewed', etc.; this supports transparency about the review process.
